execution_contract.argv: Templates are literal argv arrays, no shell, run relative to the verified arm workspace. The executable name is replaced only by its externally held resolved tool path.
execution_contract.capture: Retain exact argv/tool pins, cwd/arm, exit code and complete raw stdout/stderr plus byte lengths/SHA256. Never trim, normalize or combine streams; exceeding a bound is failure.
execution_contract.comparison: Each arm must independently match every literal exit/stream expectation; equal outputs between two wrong arms are insufficient.
execution_contract.environment: LC_ALL=C; LANG=C; TERM=dumb. No RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH or injected tool configuration. stdout/stderr are captured non-TTY byte streams; no color, line-number or filename-prefix configuration.
execution_contract.ordering: Run the operations in listed order. The three cat commands are separate sequential calls, preserving each complete source and its identity.
execution_contract.precondition: Both existing MAIN arm workspaces must already verify against their externally held workspace-manifest digests. Recheck every required source file against source_files before and after these native reads.
execution_contract.tools: Resolved pinned ripgrep rg, GNU diff and cat binaries; executor records each absolute tool identity before execution. No native tool was run to author this oracle.

nonclaims: These native-tool checks cover literal public source-byte search, reading and version comparison only.
Unchanged controller wording does not establish unchanged governing context: the preserved external definitions differ.
Declared current/prior labels do not grant authority, authenticate versions or select a governing version.
This additive oracle does not change the frozen source/workflow oracles, same core/checker, source/resource bounds, or separate adaptive-client budget.
Native source-reading freedom is not an overall32-call quota and does not reset or bypass the optional client budget.
Original workflows may use verified originals in place; no mandatory materialization cost or strongest-baseline/benefit claim is introduced.

operations.literal_basis: One complete held102-byte controller line; rg adds its output LF although the original source has no final newline.
The two held controller source byte strings are identical.
Manual one-line GNU unified diff: fixed labels, @@ -1 +1 @@ hunk, old/new complete source lines, and a no-final-newline marker after each changed line.
Complete original controller bytes, no added final LF.
Complete current-declared external definition bytes, no added final LF; declared label conveys no current authority.
Complete maintenance exception/recovery bytes, no added final LF.
